ambient_events: A box slides out of the wall somewhere down the row, then slides back. Nobody is down the row.
The shift supervisor turns a page on her clipboard, which is paper.
One of the boxes on the bottom tier is warm.
The dehumidifier cycles. Whatever's in here is being kept very dry indeed.
A brass number plate has been unscrewed and rescrewed enough times to strip the slots.
The camera at the end of the row does not sweep. It simply looks at the stairwell, always.
description: Two thousand brass-fronted doors in a room built for eight people at a time, stacked floor to ceiling down both walls in tiers, each with a number and a keyhole and absolutely no explanation. There's a viewing table in the middle under a lamp with a shade angled so the cameras can't see the tabletop, a courtesy Citadel advertises and does not, on the evidence, honour. The air is bone-dry and smells faintly of brass polish and old paper. A shift supervisor works the row with a clipboard, and does not look up when you come in, and knows precisely where you are. At the far end the floor gives way to a short flight of steel steps going down into the dark, closed off by a slab the size of a car door.
name: Citadel Financial — Safe Deposit Gallery
